title: Airstrike on Gold-Mining Camps Near Egypt Border Kills 15-30, Attribution Contested
detail: Fixed-wing aircraft and drones fired approximately four missiles and explosive bombs at artisanal gold-mining camps at Jabal al-Uqaydat and Jabal al-Ahmar, River Nile State, northeast of Atbara near the disputed Halayeb Triangle, on June 16, 2026. Casualty figures vary sharply by outlet: Darfur24 and the Sudanese Alliance for Rights reported at least 15 killed and 50+ wounded; Mada Masr and Drop Site News, citing Egyptian sources, reported 23+ killed; other secondary aggregation put the toll as high as 30 killed and 80+ injured. An estimated 5,000-7,000 informal miners fled after armored units advanced and shut down the camps. Two senior Egyptian officials told Mada Masr the operation targeted unlicensed Sudanese mining groups operating near Egyptian territory, framed as an effort to block UAE-supplied arms reaching the RSF and curb informal armed groups near the border. Attribution to Egypt was not confirmed by Cairo in initial reporting; the casualty range and attribution remain contested.
